action: Agenda slide builds up three items: approaching hairstyles, how hair grooming works in Blender, the artist's workflow.
view: full-screen slide
why: Sets out the chapter plan.

action: Slide tells the viewer to analyse the hairstyle from references, ideally from every angle, before making it.
view: full-screen slide
why: References drive the breakdown.
reader_equivalent: Collect reference pictures per side; a side with no picture cannot be measured later.

action: Checklist slide appears with the first bullet: can the hairstyle be separated into parts that are easier to groom.
view: full-screen slide
why: Question 1 of the pre-check.

action: Second bullet (flow/direction) appears, then the reference board is shown: a ponytail woman and a swept-back man in profile.
view: reference board, side views
why: Show what hairstyles to break down.

action: Draws orange arrows over the ponytail reference: strands converge at the band, the lower ponytail runs a different direction and is shorter; red outlines mark the parts.
view: side-view reference, drawn over
why: Answers question 2: flow per part.
reader_equivalent: Write the flow per part as start point, direction and gather point before placing any guide.

action: Slide states a head has about 100,000 hairs, too many to comb, so a few strands control the majority.
view: full-screen slide
why: Motivates guides plus children.

action: Animated demo plane with a few dark guide strands and many pale children, then a subdivision-surface mesh shown as the same few-control-many idea.
view: perspective of a flat plane with hair
why: Explain guide hair versus child hair.

action: Opens the course file in Sculpting workspace on a bald head; the Asset Browser is open on Essentials > Hair beside the viewport; selects the scalp object (outlined on the forehead/skull) and moves it.
view: front orthographic, matcap grey, bald head
why: Shows what a scalp object is and where the hair assets live.
reader_equivalent: hair_group(name) appends the bundled group; scalp_from_faces builds the scalp object

action: Switches to the Delete brush in Curves Sculpt Mode with Sphere on and Size about 82 px; hovers one long guide and deletes it, other guides stay.
view: front/three-quarter, guides sticking far above the head
why: Removes unwanted guides.

action: With the Select brush (Sphere, Projected, Strength 1.0 visible) hovers whole curves to select them and then returns to Comb; many long guides fan out from the head.
view: front orthographic, head at bottom, guides above
why: Select whole curves so a later brush affects only those.
reader_equivalent: reshape_guides(hair, fn) applied to chosen indices only

action: Selects a few curves, switches to Comb, pushes them sideways with a large circle (Size about 312 px, Strength 1.000 in header); then shows the Sphere/Projected pair in the header and combs the whole fan sideways.
view: front orthographic, zoomed out so the whole fan shows
why: Demonstrates Sphere vs Projected and comb direction.
reader_equivalent: reshape_guides(hair, fn) bending chosen curves toward a new direction about their roots

action: Combs the whole fan down into a rough hairdo with a very large brush (Size about 404 px, Strength 1.000), then leaves sculpt mode and selects the Curves object (all strands orange).
tool: Comb brush, then Object Mode select
view: front orthographic, then Object Mode
why: Shows the guides are one Curves object; next step adds modifiers.

action: Layout: Asset Browser on the left of the properties column showing Essentials > Hair thumbnails (Blend, Displace, Frizz, Hair Curves Noise, Roll, Rotate, Shrinkwrap, Smooth, Straighten, Trim, Duplicate, Generate, Interpolate, Braid, Clump, Create Guide Index Map, Curl, Curve Info, Curve Root, Curve Segment, Curve Tip, Attach, Redistribute).
view: front orthographic, hair on the head
why: Lists the bundled hair node groups.
reader_equivalent: hair_group(name) with the exact title shown here

action: Drags Interpolate Hair Curves from the browser onto the viewport; all hair vanishes; the modifier tab then shows Surface Deform plus Interpolate Hair Curves with Surface empty, Surface UV UVMap, Method Random, Density 10.000, Part by Mesh Islands ticked.
view: front orthographic, bald head, properties editor on Modifiers
why: Shows that Surface must be set or nothing draws.
reader_equivalent: add_hair_modifier(obj, 'Interpolate Hair Curves', Surface=scalp, Surface_UV_Map='UVMap', Poisson_Disk_Distribution=False, Density=...)

action: Adds Clump Hair Curves on top and shows its panel (Factor 1.000, Shape 0.500, Tip Spread, Guide Distance 0.1 m, Existing Guide Map ticked); the clumped hair streams swept to one side from three-quarter view.
view: three-quarter, full hair showing
why: Shows what clumping does to children.

action: Task-switcher overlay while the narrator jumps between Blender, slides and the pure-ref board; modifier stack on the hair shows four modifiers over a small node tree; then a workflow slide says this suits almost all styles.
view: Blender with node editor below viewport, then slide
why: Moves into the workflow section.

action: Title card 'Hair Grooming', then the character file opens in UV Editing: body_retopo with coloured UV islands, the hair reference panel (sketch plus two ponytail photos) beside it.
view: perspective, full body in A-pose
why: Starting point of the hair stage: retopo body with UVs.

action: Switches to Layout workspace, opens N panel View tab and sets focal length 150, then opens the Viewport Shading popover and clicks MatCap; Outline stays ticked.
tool: Layout workspace, View tab, Viewport Shading popover
view: perspective, character far away then framed
why: Clean flat view for judging hair.

action: Reference canvas pans across face, boots, skirt, top and hair panels, then lands on a pair of eyebrow-and-lash close-ups with yellow-marked hairs.
view: 2D reference canvas
why: Shows the target brow and lash look.

action: Shows a short-hair portrait reference, then the ponytail panel, then the brow/lash close-up; Blender layout viewport shows the bald character with the reference floating in a corner.
view: 2D reference, then perspective viewport
why: Plan: brows, lashes, a short cut, then the ponytail style last.

action: Drops the eyebrow close-up reference into the Layout viewport corner and enlarges it; the character head is a bald low-poly in perspective.
view: perspective, head and chest
why: Keeps the brow target visible while working.
reader_equivalent: Hold the reference pictures beside the capture; compare the brow outline to it

action: Selects the quad faces on one brow region of body_retopo (orange), then pans, zooms and finally enables the high-poly collection so the sculpted brow ridge shows through the mesh.
tool: Edit Mode face select, outliner collection toggle
view: front perspective zoomed on the brow
why: Pick the area where the brow sits, check it against the sculpt.

action: Duplicates the selected faces into brow_scalp, which carries a Shrinkwrap (Nearest Surface Point, On Surface, target body_retopo, offset 0) and Mirror modifier; Ctrl+A opens the Apply menu, picks Visual Geometry to Mesh, then moves it into a new collection.
tool: Apply menu (Visual Geometry to Mesh), Shrinkwrap, Mirror
view: front perspective, brow scalp outlined orange
why: Bakes the scalp to the surface and both sides.
reader_equivalent: scalp_from_faces(...) does the duplicate, shrinkwrap, mirror and apply

action: Selects all scalp faces, unwraps with Angle Based from the UV menu (a UV checker texture was showing first and is removed); two orange UV islands appear.
view: front perspective plus UV editor
why: Gives the scalp the UV map that Interpolate needs; pins from the body must be cleared first.

action: Scales the two UV islands down and moves them inside the square, then closes the UV editor area and returns to a full 3D view of the brow scalp.
view: UV editor beside front perspective
why: UV placement does not matter for this use.

action: Closes the timeline, confirms the scalp now has UVs and moves toward adding the Curves object; scalp outlines both brows in the front view.
view: front perspective
why: Ready to add the empty hair object.

action: Adds an Empty Hair curve object (named eyebrows in the outliner under hair_scalp, with a Surface Deform modifier), shows the high-poly head again with real brow ridge, then picks the Annotate tool and sets Placement to Surface in the tool header (3D Cursor/View/Surface offered).
tool: Add > Curve > Empty Hair; Annotate tool
view: front perspective, highpoly visible
why: Draws the brow shape on the sculpt as a guide before grooming.
reader_equivalent: decide brow centre line points from the sculpt and the reference; no Annotate needed

action: Switches to Curves Sculpt Mode; the Comb brush is active (Size 100 px, Strength 1.000, Sphere); a brush shelf with Comb, Grow/Shrink, Pinch, Puff, Pull Tips, Slide, Smooth, Add, Delete, Density, Select appears; picks Add, turns on X symmetry and drops the first strand near the brow where a blue annotation line shows.
view: front perspective then three-quarter
why: First guide of the brow; too long at default.

action: Opens the Curve Shape popover in the Add header, ticks Interpolate Radius (Length, Shape, Point Count unticked), types 0.01 into Length and leaves Points at 8, then redraws the strand much shorter.
view: front perspective then zoomed in on one brow
why: Sets the guide length to brow scale.
reader_equivalent: add_guides(..., points=8) with a flow length of about 0.007-0.01 m

action: Zoomed onto the right brow, uses the Q quick-favorites menu (Add, Delete, Comb, Grow/Shrink, Pull Tips, Smooth, Slide, Puff) and keys F and Q to change brushes; adds a second strand and combs it along the blue line with Comb at Strength 1.000, Projected.
view: front view very close to the brow, then tilted
why: Place a few guides and comb them to the brow direction.
reader_equivalent: flow_guides(body, roots, flow, length, points=8, lift=0.0005)

action: One guide pokes through the face: selects it with the Select brush, switches to Comb (Projected, Strength 1.000, Size roughly 200-300 px) and pushes it outward over the brow; the view is rotated edge-on to prove it sits above the skin; key overlay shows F and A repeated for brush swaps.
view: extreme close three-quarter, then edge-on side view of the brow
why: Fix a guide that passes through the mesh.
reader_equivalent: flow_guides(..., lift=0.0005) pushes every step above the surface

action: Combs a row of short guides along the blue annotation line toward the temple with Comb at Size about 410-470 px, mode Projected, Strength 1.000; the guides fan upward at the inner end and lean outward further along.
view: front view very close on one brow
why: Sets brow flow direction.
reader_equivalent: brow_flow(p, t) in the brow example

action: Switches to Grow/Shrink, whose header shows a Scaling popover with Scale Uniform unticked and Minimum Length 0 m; with Ctrl held it strokes along the tail end of the brow so the guides shorten toward the temple.
view: three-quarter close view of brow tail
why: Taper the brow tail.
reader_equivalent: reshape_guides(hair, lambda i,p: root + (p-root)*scale) with scale below 1 toward the tail

action: Drags Interpolate Hair Curves from the Asset Browser onto the viewport with a small text editor visible below listing the four steps (create guides, interpolate, clump, add noise and frizz); everything vanishes, then the Interpolate panel appears with Surface empty.
tool: Asset Browser drag and drop, Text editor notes
view: front perspective close on one eye and brow
why: Step 2 of the four-step workflow.

action: Picks the brow scalp as Surface with the eyedropper (UV map UVMap, Interpolation 4, Part by Mesh Islands ticked), then types a Density; orange hair bursts across the whole forehead after the value is entered.
view: front view, forehead and eyes
why: Children appear once Surface and Density are set.

action: Switches to the body in a three-quarter view, raises Density further (about 800 000 legible), brow hair swells into a big grey mass that covers the forehead on both sides; tries Alt-click on the mask texture field.
view: three-quarter then front close-up
why: Shows why a mask is needed.

action: Selects the brow_scalp object and adds a mask: picks the Texture Paint workspace-style mode, ready to paint a density image; interpolated hair still fills the whole scalp outline.
tool: Texture Paint mode, Mask Texture slot
view: front close-up, scalp outlined orange
why: Mask restricts hair to the brow shape.

action: In Texture Paint mode (brush Paint Hard) sets Mode to Single Image in the Texture Slots popover, clicks New, and types brow density in the Create New Image dialog (width and height fields visible, Blank, alpha ticked).
tool: Texture Paint, Texture Slots popover, New Image dialog
view: front close-up
why: Paint the mask as a texture.
reader_equivalent: build bpy.types.Image, fill pixels with numpy, save, pass as Mask_Texture

action: Paints white strokes on the scalp (Paint Soft, Size 44 px, Strength 1.000, Mix blend) along the brow outline; the Image Editor shows two white arcs on black; opens Image menu and picks Save.
tool: Texture Paint, Paint Soft; Image > Save
view: close view of scalp island (local view) plus Image Editor
why: Mask is saved by hand, otherwise lost.
reader_equivalent: Fill the image array white inside the brow shape, then image.save()

action: After painting, jumps back to Object Mode and zooms out: only a thin brow line of hair remains on each side of the head; painted dark patches are visible where the mask excluded hair.
view: front perspective close, then zoomed out
why: Brow hair is now confined to the mask.
reader_equivalent: hair_report(brows, body) for a strand count

action: Orbits close to the finished brow in Object Mode: hair strands appear the same thickness from root to tip, looking like thin uniform lines.
view: close-up of the brow, then very close
why: Spots that Strand display hides taper.

action: Opens the Render Properties tab (engine EEVEE, Sampling, Curves panel) and moves the mouse to the Curves Shape buttons Strand / Strip / Cylinder; Interpolate panel shows Density 1500000, Interpolation Guides 4.
view: close view of the brow, Image Editor with the mask below
why: Needed to show a radius taper.

action: Curves shape is now Strip; the brow turns into broad flat ribbons; drags Set Hair Curve Profile from the Asset Browser into the stack; its panel shows Replace Radius ticked, Radius slider, Shape 0.500, Factor Min 0.000, Factor Max 1.000; types the radius.
tool: Render > Curves Shape Strip; Set Hair Curve Profile modifier
view: close view of one brow
why: Real hair thickness and a root-to-tip taper.
reader_equivalent: add_hair_modifier(brows, 'Set Hair Curve Profile', Radius=0.0001, Shape=0.6)

action: With Radius set to 0.0001 m and Shape 0.500 the brow collapses into fine hairs; zooms in and out; after zoom out the brow shows as two thin orange selected outlines on a front view.
view: close, then front view of whole head
why: Judges realistic thickness at both scales.

action: Selects the Curves object, opens Object properties > Viewport Display and clicks the Color swatch; a colour wheel with Hex FFFFFF shows; sets it to black; brow in the viewport turns dark.
view: front view of the brow
why: Dark viewport colour reads better than the default.

action: Brow viewed three-quarter, dark: Interpolate panel with Density 3000000, Mask Texture set, Set Hair Curve Profile below; clicks the text note (step 3: clump).
view: three-quarter, head and ear
why: Brow density accepted; move to step 3.

action: Drags in Clump Hair Curves; panel shows Factor 1.000, Shape 0.500, Tip Spread 0, Clump Offset 0, Distance Falloff 0, Guide Distance, Guide Mask 1.000, Existing Guide Map ticked; scrubs Guide Distance with no change, then unticks Existing Guide Map.
view: close on the dark brow
why: Guide Distance only acts when the guide map is off.

action: Adds a second Clump Hair Curves; Guide Distance reads 0.002 m, Existing Guide Map off; hairs form a tighter clump inside the first clumps, with the brow looking bushy.
view: close view of the brow, scrubbing the dimension
why: Break the brow into sub-clumps.

action: Pulls back to see the full brow with both clumps, clicks into the notes text for step 4 (noise and frizz), and hovers on Frizz Hair Curves in the asset browser.
view: three-quarter, then close
why: Moves to noise and frizz.

action: Drops Frizz Hair Curves onto the brow; brow explodes into frizzy wire with Cumulative ticked, Factor 1.000, Distance 0.01 m, Shape 0.500 until the values are brought down; asset tooltip reads 'Frizz' hair using a random vector per point.
view: front close-up of one brow
why: Adds randomness to all strands.
reader_equivalent: add_hair_modifier(brows, 'Frizz Hair Curves', Cumulative_Offset=False, Factor=0.272, Distance=0.001, Shape=0.5)

action: Lowers Frizz Distance to 0.001 m (Cumulative unticked) and then drags the Factor value down: strands go from wild to a light fuzz; Factor field ends reading about 0.342 before settling.
view: close-up of the brow in Object Mode
why: Add a little randomness without destroying the shape.
reader_equivalent: add_hair_modifier(brows, 'Frizz Hair Curves', Cumulative_Offset=False, Factor=0.272, Distance=0.001, Shape=0.5)

action: Frizz Factor reads 0.272 with Distance 0.001 m; steps back to a full-face front view to judge the brows against the head, then keeps orbiting; the stack now lists Surface Deform, Interpolate, Set Hair Curve Profile, two Clumps and the Frizz.
view: front and three-quarter view of whole head
why: Accepts the brow look and moves on.
reader_equivalent: outline_proxy and render checks at exit

action: Starts the eyelashes: flat front view, rotates to a side view, tabs into Edit Mode on body_retopo and selects the edge ring around the eye opening; the Subdivision modifier panel shows viewport level 1, render 2.
tool: Edit Mode on body_retopo, edge/face select
view: side view of the eye, wireframe visible
why: Pick the lid ring as lash scalp.

action: Unwraps the duplicated lash scalp: UV editor shows four long curved strips; checks for overlapping duplicates and scales/moves them, then escapes; the new object lashes_scalp is outlined orange as a thin ring on both eyes.
view: front view, orange rings on both eyes; UV editor
why: Gives the lash scalp a clean UV map.

action: Add brush in Curves Sculpt Mode on the new eyelashes curve object; opens Curve Shape popover, ticks Radius, types Length about 0.01 m, Points 8; a lone pale guide appears at the lid corner; header shows Sphere, Projected, Count 1.
view: close on the eye, front/three-quarter
why: Sets lash guide length.

action: Notes the strip radius is too fat; clicks through Render Properties > Curves; the Shape row (Strand/Strip/Cylinder) is reached; hand-cursor on the lid, a small flat patch near the outer corner is the guide width.
view: close view of the eye, properties tab Render
why: Use Strand while grooming guides, Strip only to judge thickness.

action: Places lashes along the upper lid with Add; a selected scalp shows as a thin red ring so roots can be seen; keeps the count low and evenly spaced; white guides fan outward from the lid; view tilts to see them from the side.
view: three-quarter then edge-on from the side
why: Evenly spaced guides on the lid.
reader_equivalent: add_guides with roots from scalp_points(lashes_scalp, spacing=...)

action: Grow/Shrink with Ctrl held shortens lashes near the two corners (Strength 1.000, Size about 164 px, Sphere, Scaling falloff), then clicks plain Grow to lengthen the middle ones; orange ring of scalp visible along the lid.
view: three-quarter close on the eye
why: Shorter lashes at both corners, longest in the middle.

action: Front view shows lashes fanned outward on one eye; switches to Comb; the other eye is covered by X symmetry after a mirror; Q/F keystroke overlay shows brush swaps; combs the lash tips with Comb (Sphere, Projected, Size about 360 px).
view: front, then a side-on edge view of the lid, then oblique
why: Curve lashes up and outward.

action: Combs the upper lashes into a swept curve in a close three-quarter view; then enters Object Mode, selects the Curves object, and goes back to sculpt to start the lower lashes on the same object.
view: close three-quarter on the eye
why: Finish upper lashes, start lower ones.
reader_equivalent: same lash flow, shorter, pointing out and down

action: Closes the N sidebar, then follows the text note 'interpolate the guide hair'; resizes the Asset Browser wider to find Interpolate; lashes are visible as sparse guides, Curves shape still Strand.
view: front view of the head, face only
why: Moves to interpolating the lashes.

action: Switches Curves Shape to Strip, drops Set Hair Curve Profile; first it is fat (default Radius 0.01 m visible), then the Radius field is edited down; Interpolate panel shows a Density in the millions.
tool: Render > Curves Shape Strip; Set Hair Curve Profile
view: close view of the eye, flat black ribbons until Radius is lowered
why: Strip display to judge real thickness.

action: Places Set Hair Curve Profile above Interpolate in the stack (order: Surface Deform, Set Hair Curve Profile, Interpolate), then adds Clump Hair Curves; lashes clump into spiky bunches.

settings.order: Set Hair Curve Profile before Interpolate

view: three-quarter view, then close on the eye
why: Order of the profile modifier does not matter, as stated.
reader_equivalent: add_hair_modifier order: profile, interpolate, clump, noise

action: Clump panel reads Factor 1.000, Shape 0.500, Tip Spread 0.001, Guide Distance 0.001 m, Existing Guide Map off; then drops Hair Curves Noise into the stack; lashes become wispy.
tool: Clump Hair Curves, then Hair Curves Noise
view: front view of both eyes, then close on one eye
why: Roughs up the upper lashes.
reader_equivalent: add_hair_modifier(lashes, 'Clump Hair Curves', Existing_Guide_Map=False, Guide_Distance=0.001, Tip_Spread=0.001)

action: Hair Curves Noise panel shows Cumulative Offset unticked, Factor about 0.132 after dragging, Distance 0.01 m, Shape 0.500, Scale 8.980, Scale along Curve 15.000, Offset per Curve 0.000; the lash selection glows orange around the eye after.
view: close view of one eye, then front
why: Lashes look natural, not perfect.
reader_equivalent: add_hair_modifier(lashes, 'Hair Curves Noise', Cumulative_Offset=False, Factor=0.04, Shape=0.5, Scale=9.0, Scale_along_Curve=15.0)

action: Lower lashes, now the object eyelashes.001 with Surface Deform, Set Hair Curve, Interpolate (Surface lashes_scalp, Part by Mesh Islands ticked, Density about 2500000), Clump, Hair Curves Noise; viewport shows both eyes with finished lashes; stack panels collapsed to a list.
view: front and close views of the face
why: Lower lashes copied from the upper, then thinned.
reader_equivalent: a second Curves object 'eyelashes.001' on the same scalp

action: Starts the practice short cut: a floating reference portrait of a short-hair person, bald head in front/three-quarter view; stack of the lashes object is collapsed.
view: front and three-quarter of the head
why: Makes the short style match the reference.

action: Head hair scalp: in Edit Mode on body_retopo selects the cranium faces (orange region from hairline to back, shown from side, back and rear three-quarter), Shift-adds missing faces, then Shift+D duplicates and P separates.
tool: Edit Mode face select, Shift+D, P separate
view: side, back, three-quarter views with wireframe
why: Cut a scalp from the skull faces inside the hairline.

action: Ctrl+A > Visual Geometry to Mesh on the new scalp (its stack has Shrinkwrap on body_retopo and Mirror, merge 0.001 m); Tab into Edit Mode, A, U, Unwrap; one UV island appears.
tool: Apply > Visual Geometry to Mesh; U unwrap

settings.Shrinkwrap: Nearest Surface Point, On Surface, offset 0 m

view: three-quarter perspective with UV editor
why: Bake the scalp and give it UVs.

action: Renames the new scalp mesh to hair_scalp in the outliner (double-click), scalp outline hugging the skull in three-quarter view; properties panel shows Viewport Display colour white.
view: three-quarter view
why: Name the scalp before adding the Curves object.

action: Names the Curves object short, shows the reference portrait floating, switches to Curves Sculpt Mode (Comb active, Sphere, Strength 1.000); pans the reference board to the short-hair portrait to confirm the plan.
tool: Add > Curve > Empty Hair, Curves Sculpt Mode
view: three-quarter perspective, then reference canvas
why: Start of the practice short cut.

action: Density brush: header reads Distance Min about 0.01 m and Count Max 100; paints over the whole cranium from several views and fills it with straight white guides standing up like a mohawk; then types 0.02 into Distance Min to thin them.
view: side view, top-down view, then side again
why: Fill the scalp quickly, then thin if too dense.

action: Combs the standing guides down at the sides and back (Comb, Projected, Falloff Curve) from a side view, keeps hairs in front of the ear, and checks hairs aren't passing over the ear; keys F and Q switch brushes.
view: side view, then close on the ear
why: Short hair lies down along the head.
reader_equivalent: flow_guides(body, roots, flow, length=0.04, points=8, lift=0.003)

action: Looks at the head from above and the front, then combs fringe hairs forward and upward at the front hairline following the reference; Size about 230 px visible in the on-screen label.
view: top, then three-quarter front
why: Front flicks match the portrait.
reader_equivalent: a flow with +Z and -Y components at the front roots

action: Guides finished (swept, orange when selected, from the side). Switches to Object Mode, then picks the Geometry Node editor to build the hair as a node tree rather than modifiers; asset browser shows the full Essentials > Hair list.
view: side view, orange guides
why: Choose nodes over modifiers for more control.

action: Changes the lower area to the Geometry Node Editor through the editor-type menu; a Surface Deform group node tree shows (Group Input to Surface Deform.002 to Group Output); resizes the area.
view: side view of head with node editor below
why: Existing Surface Deform modifier is left alone.
reader_equivalent: do not touch the Surface Deform modifier

action: Adds a new node tree called short hair on the short object; drags Set Hair Curve Profile into it between Group Input and Group Output; viewport shows the hair as Strip ribbons; types 0.1 mm into the Radius field.
tool: Geometry nodes: Set Hair Curve Profile
view: front and three-quarter, node editor below
why: Real thickness before interpolating.

action: Zooms into the node: Radius 0.0001 m, Shape 0.500; brings the head to a back view where guides look thin; drags Interpolate Hair Curves from the asset browser into the node tree after the profile node.
view: back view, thin guides, node editor below
why: Step 2 as nodes.
reader_equivalent: hair_tree(...) interp node linked after profile

action: Interpolate node settings (Part by Mesh Islands ticked, Interpolation Guides 4, Distance to Guides 0 m, Method Random, Density 800000, Density Mask 1.000, Viewport Amount 1.000) with a dense dark hair cap on the back of the head; combs hair over the nape in a back view.
tool: Interpolate Hair Curves node; Comb brush
view: back view and nape close-ups
why: See the children and comb the nape.

action: Clump node expanded: Guide Distance 0.05 m, Existing Guide Map unticked, Guide Index socket; double-clicks Guide Distance and types 0.01; the hair on top breaks into definite clumps with a visible forward fringe, then a front view of the finished short cut.
view: three-quarter front then front view
why: Break hair into clumps.

action: In the clump node drags Factor from about 0.994 down to 0.765 so the bunches soften; Guide Map shows Guide Distance 0.015 m, Existing Guide Map unticked; the hair on top becomes dense with visible clumps from above and the side.
view: three-quarter then top-down close, node editor below
why: Soften the primary clump.

action: Pulls out the node tree to show a longer chain (profile, interpolate with Named Attribute for the UV map, clump, Create Guide Index Map, Delete Geometry, noise); Interpolate Density reads 1000000-1500000; viewport Strength 1.000 Comb at Size 242 px nudges strands.
view: side view then three-quarter, nodes below
why: Check hair after secondary clump.

action: Hair Curves Noise node expanded: Cumulative Offset unticked, Factor 1.000, Distance 0.015 m, Shape 0.500, Scale 31.500, Scale along Curve 15.400, Offset per Curve 0.000; adds Separate Geometry; note overlay says change Domain from Point to Spline.
tool: Hair Curves Noise node, Separate Geometry node
view: close hair and node editor maximised
why: Put noise on only part of the hair.

action: Adds a Random Value node (Boolean) feeding Separate Geometry Selection, types Probability 0.25 (a field reading 0.250 or similar); hair on top becomes partly rough, partly smooth.
view: nodes maximised, then three-quarter hair view
why: Noise on a quarter of the strands.

action: Final short cut: Interpolate shows Density 1500000, Part by Mesh Islands ticked, Interpolation Guides 4; the full node graph is a long chain from Set Hair Curve Profile to Join Geometry; from side and front the cut looks like the reference.
view: front, side, then node graph zoomed out
why: Wrap-up of the practice style.
reader_equivalent: density=1500000 in hair_tree for the final style, 800000 for the practice

action: Back to the reference canvas to analyse the ponytail style: pans to the hair panel with the sketch and two reference photos (profile and three-quarter) and draws on it; main parts are outlined.
view: 2D reference, then blown up
why: Analyse before grooming.

action: Annotate tool set to Surface: draws blue lines on the bald head to mark the parting pattern and hairline pattern; header shows Placement Surface; reference photos float in the viewport; Add brush with Curve Shape set before first strand.
view: front, top, then wire-overlay views of the cranium
why: Mark the hair pattern before placing guides.
reader_equivalent: decide parting line world points from the reference

action: Opens Add brush Curve Shape popover: Interpolate Radius ticked, Length about 0.3 m, Points set to 30 (field being typed); keeps X symmetry on; drops a first long guide from the hairline in the middle, shown as a long dark ribbon in the air.
